key_findings: The lower stair flight overlaps the saved 2.35 m landing by approximately 0.43 m along its run.
The upper stair flight overlaps the saved 2.75 m landing by approximately 0.56 m along its run.
Both saved landings also overlap the saved west gallery floor mesh at the corresponding level; the connected route is still schematic because no measured interior plan is available.
The cutaway script also creates temporary path strips for the render, but the main landing-to-floor overlaps are present in saved geometry.
Five reclaimed-display-column groups are present: two ground, two third-floor, one south stairwell.
The facade/entrance and material scores remain below threshold despite the improved gallery connection.
limitations: Campus-map FID 213 is not a surveyed wall line; previous footprint metrics do not prove as-built dimensions.
The independent asset grade does not verify master placement or campus-neighbor alignment.
Roof, tower, window surround, interior dimensions, reclaimed-column positions, and stair routing remain estimated or schematic.
The evidence render uses temporary path strips; the separate fresh-reopen geometry bounds confirm saved floor/landing overlaps, but the routes are not verified as-built.
priority_fixes: Refine the portico and integrate its moulds with the building wall/roof composition using reference-supported details.
Improve window rhythm and facade articulation without inventing unsupported variation.
Improve tonal depth and material response of slate, brick, and limestone under neutral daylight.
Produce a clear section render with saved gallery floors visible and temporary explanatory overlays clearly distinguished.
